thread.title: Is this a good opportunity to buy Apple shares?

author: Admin
title: Is this a good opportunity to buy Apple shares?
text: Is this a good opportunity to buy Apple shares?   Apple (AAPL) reported both sales and profits above market expectations for the quarter ended in December 2017. However, iPhone sales measured in units showed a small year-on-year decline, which generated disappointment among investors. In this context, the shares of the company accumulate a decline of about 13% from the highs of the year. On the other hand, a detailed analysis of the numbers indicates that the evolution of demand in the iPhone segment is not as weak as the reports indicate. In addition, the firm’s business enjoys very good health on an aggregate scale, and the valuation of its shares is clearly attractive. Are we facing a purchase opportunity in the shares of Apple? A solid business The total sales of Apple during the last quarter amounted to 88,300 million dollars, which represents a growth rate of 13% year-on-year. Earnings per share increased by 16% compared to the same quarter in the previous year. Both sales and earnings exceeded analysts’ forecasts, and also set new historical highs for the company. The sales in the iPhone segment, the main business of the company, grew 13% year-on-year, mainly due to higher prices for models such as the iPhone X. However, the number of units sold decreased by 1%, and this was the main factor of negativity in the last earnings report. On the other hand, it is important to bear in mind that the quarter ended in December 2017 includes 13 weeks, while the quarter ended in December 2016 included 14 weeks. A simple mathematical projection would indicate that in a quarter of 14 weeks Apple would have reported a growth in the units sold of the iPhone. In addition, the iPhone X was available at the beginning of November in the market. Therefore, the company’s main launch in the period was absent for a good part of the quarter. That is to say, the fall in the units sold of iPhone seems to be related to seasonal issues and the dates of availability of the product, not necessarily with a weakness in demand. Analyzing the business on an aggregate scale, the data indicates that Apple is in very good health. The company has 1,300 million devices in operation worldwide, a new historical record for the company and growing 30% in two years. In addition, the services segment has become a particularly attractive growth engine for the technology firm, ranking second in terms of billing amounts behind the iPhone. The turnover in this segment grew by 18% during the last quarter, reaching 8,500 million dollars. The amount of subscriptions paid to the different services of the company amounts to 240 million, a growth of 30 million new subscriptions in a period of 90 days. Also, the company has 163,000 million dollars in cash or cash and liquid assets in the balance, and the tax reform in the United States gives you the opportunity to repatriate much of that money. Apple will announce its new capital allocation plan in the next results report, although it would seem that the company’s shareholders will be rewarded with an increase in capital distributions through dividends and medium-term share repurchases. Valuation and key price levels to take into account After the recent price decline, we can identify three key levels as possible support for the quotes. In the first place, the area of ​​150 dollars per share worked as price support in August and September of 2017, and represents a relevant area in the short term. In the event of a downward break, we can identify a second level of possible price support in the area close to $142 per share, a level that acted as support during April, May and June of last year. Regarding bullish objectives, in the short term the 162 area per share is relevant, which worked as a support in September of last year. In the event of a sustained break above that level, the possibility of a recovery of the historical maximums for Apple in the vicinity of 180 dollars per unit is enabled. It is interesting to note that the valuation of Apple shares is quite attractive. The company is quoted at a price-earnings ratio of 16.45 times the firm’s results in the last year. In comparison, the average of the companies in the S & P 500 index trades at a price-earnings ratio in the area of ​​23.6. To a large extent, this below-average valuation may be due to sales instability in the iPhone segment, since companies in the consumer electronics industry tend to trade at relatively low valuations because they operate in a particularly cyclical industry. unstable. With this in mind, Apple’s ability to sustain sales and increasing profits over time is key, beyond the oscillations in the industry. In the event that the company can bring peace of mind to investors about its ability to generate sales and profits in long-term expansion, its shares could offer attractive bullish potential from current price levels. On average, Wall Street analysts have a target price of $192.63 for Apple’s shares, which implies a revaluation potential of about 24% from current levels. TAGS
